claims.title: Reign of Gorm the Old at Jelling
claims.summary: Gorm the Old, the first historically recognised king of Denmark, ruled from Jelling in Jutland and raised the older Jelling stone in memory of his wife Thyra, founding the royal line that endures today.

sources.label: Gorm the Old, Harald Bluetooth and Svein Forkbeard

claims.title: The Jelling Stone names Denmark
claims.summary: King Harald Bluetooth raised a great rune-stone at Jelling proclaiming that he had unified Denmark and Norway and made the Danes Christian; it carries the earliest written record of the name Denmark.

sources.label: Jelling Mounds, Runic Stones and Church

claims.title: Christianization of the Danes
claims.summary: Harald Bluetooth accepted Christianity around 965, the official start of Denmark's conversion, binding the new kingdom to Latin Christendom and to the wider culture of medieval Europe.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Denmark: From the rune-stone kingdom of the Vikings to a Scandinavian monarchy that shed its empire and remade itself as a modern welfare state.", terralore.co/country/DNK/chronicle#ev-965-christianization-of-the-danes, claim TL:DNK:event:965:christianization-of-the-danes, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Cnut the Great and the North Sea empire
claims.summary: Cnut won the English throne in 1016, inherited Denmark in 1018 and conquered Norway in 1028, ruling a maritime empire across the North Sea until his death in 1035.

sources.label: Gorm the Old, Harald Bluetooth and Svein Forkbeard

claims.title: The Kalmar Union
claims.summary: At Kalmar the magnates of Denmark, Norway and Sweden crowned Erik of Pomerania as common king under the regency of Margaret I, uniting the three Scandinavian kingdoms in a single monarchy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Denmark: From the rune-stone kingdom of the Vikings to a Scandinavian monarchy that shed its empire and remade itself as a modern welfare state.", terralore.co/country/DNK/chronicle#ev-1397-the-kalmar-union, claim TL:DNK:event:1397:the-kalmar-union, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The rule of Margaret I
claims.summary: Margaret I governed Denmark, Norway and Sweden as their effective ruler from the late 1380s until her death in 1412, the architect and guarantor of the Kalmar Union.

sources.label: Denmark: Margaret I and the Kalmar Union

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Denmark: From the rune-stone kingdom of the Vikings to a Scandinavian monarchy that shed its empire and remade itself as a modern welfare state.", terralore.co/country/DNK/chronicle#ev-1387-the-rule-of-margaret-i, claim TL:DNK:event:1387:the-rule-of-margaret-i, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Stockholm Bloodbath
claims.summary: King Christian II's execution of Swedish nobles after his coronation in Stockholm inflamed Swedish resistance and helped precipitate the collapse of the Kalmar Union.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Denmark: From the rune-stone kingdom of the Vikings to a Scandinavian monarchy that shed its empire and remade itself as a modern welfare state.", terralore.co/country/DNK/chronicle#ev-1520-the-stockholm-bloodbath, claim TL:DNK:event:1520:the-stockholm-bloodbath, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sweden leaves the union
claims.summary: Gustav Vasa's rising drove out Danish rule and led to Sweden's secession from the Kalmar Union, leaving Denmark joined to Norway alone.

sources.label: Denmark: Margaret I and the Kalmar Union

claims.title: The Reformation under Christian III
claims.summary: After winning the Count's War, Christian III dissolved the authority of the Catholic bishops and established a Lutheran state church, making Denmark-Norway a Protestant realm and strengthening the crown.

sources.label: Christian III, king of Denmark and Norway

claims.title: The long wars with Sweden
claims.summary: From the Northern Seven Years' War onward, Denmark and Sweden fought repeatedly for control of the Baltic and the Sound, a rivalry that steadily eroded Danish power in the region.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Denmark: From the rune-stone kingdom of the Vikings to a Scandinavian monarchy that shed its empire and remade itself as a modern welfare state.", terralore.co/country/DNK/chronicle#ev-1563-the-long-wars-with-sweden, claim TL:DNK:event:1563:the-long-wars-with-sweden, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Treaty of Roskilde
claims.summary: After Sweden's invasion across the frozen belts, Denmark ceded Scania, Halland, Blekinge, Bornholm and Trondheim; the loss of the eastern provinces was the largest in Danish history.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Denmark: From the rune-stone kingdom of the Vikings to a Scandinavian monarchy that shed its empire and remade itself as a modern welfare state.", terralore.co/country/DNK/chronicle#ev-1658-treaty-of-roskilde, claim TL:DNK:event:1658:treaty-of-roskilde, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The establishment of absolutism
claims.summary: In the crisis following defeat by Sweden, Frederick III secured a hereditary and absolute monarchy, a system later codified in the Royal Law (Kongeloven) of 1665.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Denmark: From the rune-stone kingdom of the Vikings to a Scandinavian monarchy that shed its empire and remade itself as a modern welfare state.", terralore.co/country/DNK/chronicle#ev-1660-the-establishment-of-absolutism, claim TL:DNK:event:1660:the-establishment-of-absolutism, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The bombardment of Copenhagen
claims.summary: To stop the Danish fleet falling to Napoleon, a British force bombarded Copenhagen and carried off the navy, driving Denmark into alliance with France and toward ruin in the Napoleonic Wars.

sources.label: A Guide to the History of Recognition, Diplomatic, and Consular Relations: Denmark
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: Treaty of Kiel: the loss of Norway
claims.summary: Defeated alongside Napoleon, Denmark ceded Norway to Sweden, ending a four-century union, while keeping Iceland, the Faroe Islands and Greenland.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Denmark: From the rune-stone kingdom of the Vikings to a Scandinavian monarchy that shed its empire and remade itself as a modern welfare state.", terralore.co/country/DNK/chronicle#ev-1814-treaty-of-kiel-the-loss-of-norway, claim TL:DNK:event:1814:treaty-of-kiel-the-loss-of-norway, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The June Constitution
claims.summary: Frederick VII signed the Grundlov, abolishing absolute monarchy and establishing a constitutional government with an elected parliament; 5 June is celebrated as Constitution Day.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Denmark: From the rune-stone kingdom of the Vikings to a Scandinavian monarchy that shed its empire and remade itself as a modern welfare state.", terralore.co/country/DNK/chronicle#ev-1849-the-june-constitution, claim TL:DNK:event:1849:the-june-constitution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Danish Golden Age
claims.summary: In the decades after the loss of Norway, Denmark experienced a flowering of philosophy, science, art and literature, from Soren Kierkegaard to Hans Christian Andersen and the physicist H. C. Orsted.

sources.label: The history of Denmark: From vikings to social welfare state
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Denmark (denmark.dk)

claims.title: The Second Schleswig War
claims.summary: Prussian and Austrian armies invaded after Denmark sought to incorporate Schleswig; following defeat at Dybbol, Denmark ceded Schleswig, Holstein and Lauenburg, losing about a third of its territory.

sources.label: German-Danish War: War and the final settlement of the Schleswig-Holstein question

claims.title: Cession of the duchies
claims.summary: By the peace ending the German-Danish War, Denmark surrendered the duchies to Prussia and Austria, placing tens of thousands of Danes under German rule and reshaping the southern frontier.

sources.label: German-Danish War: War and the final settlement of the Schleswig-Holstein question

claims.title: The Schleswig plebiscites
claims.summary: Under the Treaty of Versailles, Zone 1 (Northern Schleswig) voted about 75 per cent for Denmark and Zone 2 about 80 per cent for Germany, determining where the new border would run.

sources.label: German-Danish War: War and the final settlement of the Schleswig-Holstein question

claims.title: Reunification of Northern Schleswig
claims.summary: Northern Schleswig came under Danish sovereignty on 15 June 1920, marked by King Christian X's ceremonial ride across the old frontier; the boundary then fixed remains the Danish-German border today.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Denmark: From the rune-stone kingdom of the Vikings to a Scandinavian monarchy that shed its empire and remade itself as a modern welfare state.", terralore.co/country/DNK/chronicle#ev-1920-reunification-of-northern-schleswig, claim TL:DNK:event:1920:reunification-of-northern-schleswig, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Eastern Greenland case
claims.summary: The Permanent Court of International Justice ruled that Denmark held sovereignty over the whole of Greenland, rejecting Norway's occupation of the eastern coast and confirming Danish title to the island.

sources.label: Legal Status of Eastern Greenland (Denmark v. Norway), Judgment, 5 April 1933

claims.title: German occupation of Denmark
claims.summary: Germany invaded on 9 April 1940 and Denmark surrendered within hours; a policy of negotiation gave way in August 1943 to direct German control and an active resistance movement.

sources.label: A Guide to the History of Recognition, Diplomatic, and Consular Relations: Denmark
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: Rescue of the Danish Jews
claims.summary: Warned of a German round-up, Danes spirited more than 7,000 Jews across the sound to neutral Sweden, saving the great majority of the country's Jewish population from deportation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Denmark: From the rune-stone kingdom of the Vikings to a Scandinavian monarchy that shed its empire and remade itself as a modern welfare state.", terralore.co/country/DNK/chronicle#ev-1943-rescue-of-the-danish-jews, claim TL:DNK:event:1943:rescue-of-the-danish-jews, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding member of NATO
claims.summary: Abandoning its old neutrality after the occupation, Denmark became one of the twelve founding members of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization in 1949.

sources.label: A Guide to the History of Recognition, Diplomatic, and Consular Relations: Denmark
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: Accession to the European Communities
claims.summary: After a 1972 referendum, Denmark joined the European Communities on 1 January 1973, the forerunner of the European Union and a foundation of its modern foreign policy.

sources.label: The history of Denmark: From vikings to social welfare state
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Denmark (denmark.dk)

claims.title: Hans Island agreement with Canada
claims.summary: Denmark and Canada settled the 'Whisky War' by dividing Hans Island in the Kennedy Channel, ending a dispute dating to 1973 and creating Denmark's only land border with North America.
